claims.text: Changing elemental ratios by decreasing Fe/Co and/or increasing Ti will reduce the saturation magnetization of a non-equiatomic HEA.
Ti promotes antiferromagnetic coupling in the proposed alloy system.
Reducing saturation magnetization through compositional adjustment enhances magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Enhanced magnetocrystalline anisotropy increases the coercive field.
Enhanced magnetocrystalline anisotropy shifts magnetic transition temperatures.
Changes in coercivity and magnetic transition temperatures can produce a larger magnetic entropy change or adiabatic temperature change.
FeCoNiTi alloys can contain an fcc phase.
The proposed initial non-equiatomic FeCoNiTi-like alloy has a predominantly single-phase fcc microstructure.
The proposed initial alloy has moderate saturation magnetization and moderate magnetocaloric performance.
Arc melting followed by rapid quenching is an applicable processing route for as-cast FeCoNiTi alloys.
The proposed melting or quenching processing produces homogeneous microstructures.
FeCoNiTi alloys can be magnetically characterized from room temperature through moderately elevated temperatures under applied fields.
Compositionally tuning the alloy can preserve a single-phase high-entropy solid solution while altering elemental distribution.
Modified elemental distribution produces enhanced antiferromagnetic coupling and modified magnetic clusters.
FeCoNiTi-based alloys can exhibit multiple ferromagnetic transition temperatures associated with different phases.
The fcc phase of FeCoNiTi can exhibit a high coercive field.
The tuned alloy will have higher coercivity than the baseline alloy.
The tuned alloy will have a shifted ferromagnetic transition temperature relative to the baseline.
The tuned alloy will exhibit an enhanced magnetocaloric effect relative to the baseline.
Phase separation or loss of microstructural homogeneity may negate the proposed magnetic and magnetocaloric improvements.
